subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Baked Coffee: The Silent Defect
description: A quick win: understand Baked Coffee: The Silent Defect.

hook.text: Baked coffee looks fine. It smells okay. But the cup is flat, lifeless, and dull. It's the hardest defect to diagnose.

buildup.text: Baking happens when temperature stalls or rises too slowly during the roast. The rate of rise flattens or even dips.

discovery.text: Without momentum, Maillard reactions slow down. Flavors develop incompletely—like bread pulled from the oven too early.

twist.text: Baked coffee is extremely common. Many commercial roasters produce it without realizing because it passes basic quality checks.

climax.text: The fix is ensuring a steady, declining RoR through the roast—never letting momentum stall, especially after first crack.

punchline.text: It looks roasted. It smells roasted. But the cup is dead. That's baking.

quiz.question: What causes 'baked' coffee?
options: Temperature stalling or rising too slowly—rate of rise flattens
